items.detail: Laguna files one application per scope off one complete plan set, each with its own description and valuation. The baseline scopes are: new SFR/addition/remodel with site work and grading of 20 CY or less outside the building footprint; demolition; ADU/JADU; grading of more than 20 CY outside the building footprint; and pool/spa. Each ADU or JADU normally has its own permit, but a JADU may ride with the main house; main house + JADU + ADU is two applications. Demolishing a unit requires its own demolition permit; demo-only normally also needs a construction submittal on file or Building Official approval. GRADING TEST: count only grading OUTSIDE the building footprint, using the greater of cut or fill. More than 20 CY outside the footprint needs its own grading application, valuation, permit and plan submittal; 20 CY or less rides with construction. Grading inside the footprint never counts toward the 20 CY, though it still gets review and a fee. Apply the test in one of three cases. (1) The plans or application state the inside and outside quantities: apply the test to the outside quantity. Evidence of outside grading includes grading or civil sheets, a referenced civil grading plan that is not in the packet, site or retaining walls, a new driveway or pad cut, and a subterranean garage or basement whose excavation extends beyond the footprint. Decide which case applies by reading the plans; never from a keyword. Shoring may issue with grading, but the plan checker decides which permit carries it. A house with an ADU may share one plan check but issues as two permits, one per address. Application pages may be combined into one PDF. When the City record for the named permit is available, compare its description with this filing's scope, the way a Planning record is compared: a grading record opened for another permit's work does not cover this filing's grading.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Digital Plan Submittal Guide (E-Plan), "Building Permit Application(s)"; Laguna Beach 2026 Building Requirement Sheet, GENERAL INFORMATION row 4

items.detail: "Planning approval must be completed prior to Building submittal (if required)." Laguna sequences the lanes: the Building packet is filed after the Planning entitlement or design review is approved, not alongside it. A packet can carry affirmative evidence that an approval exists — a DRB or CDP reference, a conditions sheet, a plan-check redline naming the approved plans — and that evidence is supporting, never conclusive. No packet can show that no Planning record exists. A reroof is (B)(2)(e) exterior work (Administrative Design Review, not Design Review, when the roof is white or light colored and may glare — LBMC 25.05.040(B)(3)(a)(ix) — or when the roof changes dimension, square footage or pitch — (B)(3)(a)(x); Ord. 1732), and Planning reviews every reroof.

applies_when.question: Does any exact City soils-report trigger apply: new construction, except an ADU (new, attached, or a conversion), which is not new construction here and needs this report only for a lot slope over 20%, a deep foundation (grade beams or piles), or a retaining wall over 5 ft, and is omitted when none of those apply; an SFR addition over 1,200 square feet, a new upper floor, or at least 50 percent total floor-area increase; retaining wall over 5 feet or supporting surcharge; shoring over 6 feet of cut; slope steeper than 1V:2H; beach/ocean front, coastal bluff top, steep hillside or liquefaction site; prior soil/structure failure; nonconventional foundation; qualifying new pool; or a Building Official determination?

applies_when.if_no: No Laguna soils report is submitted under this handout. This negative is about the report list only and does not decide peer review.

items.detail: Submit two bounded copies for paper intake, dated within one year of submittal. The report trigger list is broader than peer review: any new construction; an SFR addition over 1,200 square feet, a new upper floor, or total floor-area increase of 50 percent or more; a retaining wall over 5 feet or supporting surcharge; shoring over 6 feet of cut; a lot steeper than 1 vertical to 2 horizontal; construction at a beach/ocean front, coastal bluff top, steep hillside or liquefaction zone; soil or structure failure; a nonconventional foundation; a new pool on an ungraded lot, flood plain or coastal bluff top; or a Building Official determination. Do not substitute the separate peer-review list. An ADU (new, attached, or a conversion) is not "any new construction" on this list: it needs this report only for a lot slope over 20%, a deep foundation (grade beams or piles), or a retaining wall over 5 ft.

scopes.label: Residential major remodel or structural alteration

applies_when.question: Does the project meet any WQMP threshold: at least 10,000 square feet impervious area; at least 5,000 square feet and redevelopment; at least 5,000 square feet and lot slope at least 25 percent; or at least 2,500 square feet and within/adjacent to an ESA? Also identify the form's separate 200-foot WQESA direct-discharge and LID-checklist answers.
applies_when.if_yes: Submit the WQMP with the grading/drainage, street-improvement, erosion-control, geotechnical and hydrology companion plans.
applies_when.if_no: No WQMP is required by the four published numeric thresholds; preserve the separate WQESA and LID answers for Water Quality routing.

items.detail: A WQMP is required at 10,000 square feet or more of impervious area; at 5,000 square feet or more for a redevelopment; at 5,000 square feet or more on a lot with at least 25 percent slope; or at 2,500 square feet or more when within or adjacent to an ESA. The form separately asks whether the property is within 200 feet of and directly discharges to a WQESA/beach front, and whether a LID checklist is required before permitting. A triggered WQMP submittal includes grading and drainage, street improvement and erosion-control plans, a geotechnical report and a hydrology study. The conflicting $5,000 versus $1,700 plus $233 deposit statements are deliberately not encoded here.

source.citation: Laguna Beach WQMP thresholds table and WQMP submittal form, Section C

items.label: Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance (WELO) documentation

scopes.label: Residential major remodel or structural alteration

applies_when.question: Did Planning call out WELO (prescriptive or performative) on the ZPC notes for THIS work? If the notes are silent or unclear, also say whether the cover sheet or landscape sheet states a landscape area that could meet a 23 CCR section 491(a) threshold — 500 sq. ft. or more of new landscape, or 2,500 sq. ft. or more of existing landscape area. Landscape area is irrigated planting, turf and water features only (section 490.2(a)(41)).
applies_when.if_yes: Staff look up the Planning record. Record the Planning call when it is clear (prescriptive or performative). Cover-sheet landscape area rides along as supporting evidence.
applies_when.if_no: Planning clearly did not call WELO for this work, and the packet does not state a landscape area that could meet a section 491(a) threshold. Omit. A rehabilitated landscape of 1,768.7 sq. ft. is below the 2,500 sq. ft. section 491(a)(2) threshold and is supporting context only.

items.detail: The published thresholds remain the legal context and match current MWELO at 23 CCR section 491(a), effective 2025-01-02 (the same state text was numbered section 490.1 before that amendment; section 490.1 is now General Provisions): (a)(1) a NEW CONSTRUCTION project — a new building with a landscape area, or another new landscape project — with a landscape area of 500 sq. ft. or more requiring a building permit, plan check or design review; (a)(2) a REHABILITATED LANDSCAPE project with a modified landscape area of 2,500 sq. ft. or more. Section 490.2(a)(41) defines landscape area as the irrigated planting, turf and water-feature areas only; it excludes building and structure footprints, hardscape, and non-irrigated areas. Section 491(b) lets any project at or under 2,500 sq. ft. of landscape area choose the prescriptive option in section 492 rather than the performance path.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Water Efficient Landscape Requirements Information Guide, Applicability (Chapter 19.01; effective 2016-02-01)

items.label: Deferred submittals are identified on the cover sheet

items.detail: Fire sprinklers, structural roof trusses and elevators may be legitimate deferred submittals. The cover sheet must identify each deferred item, and it must be submitted, approved and separately permitted before framing inspection. Life-safety items other than fire sprinklers and roof trusses are not eligible. The deferred package itself goes through full plan review when it arrives, never over-the-counter: the City lists roof trusses (for deferred submittal) and elevators among its full plan review submittal projects.

source.citation: Laguna Beach New and Major Building Submittal Requirements (2025), "Deferred Submittal"; Laguna Beach 2026 Building Requirement Sheet, GENERAL INFORMATION row 2; Laguna Beach Building Plan Review Services (06/08/2026), Plan Review Submittal Projects; Residential: "Roof Trusses (for deferred submittal)" and "Elevator"

items.label: Residential automatic-sprinkler documentation or a valid Laguna deferral

applies_when.question: Is an automatic sprinkler system actually required for this work? A new primary dwelling is required to be sprinklered (CRC R309.2 as amended by LBMC 14.52.030). An ADU is required to be sprinklered ONLY when the primary residence is sprinklered or is being sprinklered by this project — Government Code section 66314(d)(12) and LBMC 25.17.010(f)(3) (Urgency Ord. 1713). Read the cover sheet's existing-sprinkler statement for the primary residence before answering.
applies_when.if_yes: Submit the sprinkler design or the Laguna deferred-submittal cover note committing to approval and a separate permit before framing inspection.
applies_when.if_no: No sprinkler documentation is required.

items.detail: Show the applicable sprinkler design or exception. The cover still states whether sprinklers exist and carries the notation "FIRE SPRINKLERS REQUIRED" when applicable. An ADU is exempt when the primary residence has no automatic sprinkler system: Government Code section 66314(d)(12) forbids conditioning an ADU permit on installing sprinklers that are not required for the primary dwelling, and LBMC 25.17.010(f)(3) (Urgency Ord.

source.citation: Laguna Beach New and Major Building Submittal Requirements (2025), "FIRE SPRINKLER PLANS (DEFERRED SUBMITTAL)" and "Deferred Submittal"; Laguna Beach 2026 Building Requirement Sheet, GENERAL INFORMATION row 2

Before canvassing, the Building Official approves the notice; the contractor then canvasses neighbors within 300 feet (plus any added by the official), and the owner, contractor and architect sign the acknowledgement before permit issuance. items.detail: The deliverable is the City's Building Permit Application page. The City asks for two things about it: that it is complete and that the project address on it is correct. Complete means the form's own blocks are filled — the description of work, the valuation, and the applicant, owner and contractor blocks the form prints. An accurate address matters more here than on a plan-checked project, because an OTC permit can issue the same day against whatever address the application carries. A blank block that applies to the project makes the application incomplete: the description of work, the valuation, and the contractor block on a contractor-pulled permit. A block that does not apply to the project may be blank — the architect and engineer blocks on a job with no design professional, the contractor block on an owner-builder permit — and a blank there is not a defect.

Do not rebuild the City's file-category taxonomy. The City also uses a reference slot for original stamped sets — decide from the document whether this file is this filing's working drawings or an archived original set. items.detail: Judge the file, not the portal slot. The working drawings contain a floor plan (or, on a scope with no interior work such as a fence or a sign, the drawing that locates the work on the structure or the site), and that drawing locates two things: what exists and what is proposed. Locating is the test — the reviewer must be able to point at the sheet and say where each item of work happens. items.detail: Where the work includes structural modification of a building or deck, the City's published item is stamped and signed engineered plans and calculations. Split that item at intake. The intake deliverable is the engineered DRAWINGS: plan sheets stamped and signed by the California-registered design professional who prepared them. Judge the file, not the portal slot. The City writes "(if applicable)", and the qualified-projects list says what makes it applicable: items 2 and 3 both read "with minor structural modifications". Item 10 is a wood or metal fence: its ordinary posts and footings are the trade, not this trigger. Item 11 admits only "Commercial signs without structural alterations"; the handout does not say a sign's own posts, footing or mounting are non-structural, so a sign whose support or attachment alters a structure is outside item 11 and is a structural question, not an exclusion. A wall filed against the City's unmodified Standard Block Wall Detail is answered by that bulletin's own row, not this one. A stamp and a signature are part of the drawings deliverable: an unstamped sheet is not engineered drawings.

applies_when.question: Does this reroof tear off any of the existing roofing, including a partial tear-off of one roof section, or is it an overlay over the existing material with nothing removed?

items.detail: Two deliverables, not one: the Waste Management Plan, and a separate security deposit paid by check or cash. items.label: Dimensioned schematic site plan
items.detail: The site plan is fully dimensioned and drawn to scale. It also carries project information: the project address, the owner's information, and a scope-of-work statement. The City exempts single-family, duplex and ADU installations from this sheet entirely.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Code Compliance Checklist; Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging, "Schematic Site Plan (Not required for single-family, duplex or ADU)"; Multi-Family and Non-Residential Eligibility Checklists, "Site Plan and Single Line Drawing" (documents 5111, 11685 and 11683; verified live 2026-08-20)

source.citation: Laguna Beach Code Compliance Checklist; Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging, "Disconnecting Means" citing CEC §§ 625.42 and 110.25; Multi-Family and Non-Residential Eligibility Checklists item C citing CEC § 625.43 (documents 5111, 11685 and 11683; verified live 2026-08-20)

checklists.title: Fences, block walls and retaining walls

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

items.label: Wall height above adjacent grade and distance to the property line shown

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

items.detail: The plan dimensions the wall height measured from adjacent grade and the distance from the wall to each property line. These two numbers decide whether a permit is required at all — over 30 inches from adjacent grade, or any height within three feet of a property line — so a drawing that omits either cannot be screened. The bulletin also limits the grade difference across the wall to a maximum 6-inch offset with no surcharge loads, which the same dimensions establish. The bulletin's 30-inch line and LBMC 14.50.022's 72-inch exemption disagree for a freestanding block wall between 30 and 72 inches set more than three feet from every property line and the right-of-way; that band is UNSETTLED with the City (see the prose above).

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTES 2 and 3: "Concrete block wall over 30\" in height measured from adjacent grade shall require a building permit" and "Concrete block wall in any height within three (3) feet of the property lines shall require a building permit" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27); LBMC 14.50.022, Building item 1: "Walls and fences not over 72 inches high, unless located within three feet of a property line or public right-of-way" are exempt from permit

items.label: Zoning/Planning Division approval of the wall plans

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

items.detail: The Zoning/Planning Division regulates the wall's height and location based on the zone, its position on the property, and community design standards, and approves the plans before any permit issues. Laguna sequences the two lanes here exactly as it does for buildings: the Planning approval exists first, and the Building packet is filed against the plans Planning approved.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 8: "Zoning/Planning division must approve the plans prior to any permit being issued" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Standard detail followed exactly, or plans by a registered design professional

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Does this wall follow the City's standard detail without modification, on a site under 10 percent slope with no adverse soil conditions?
applies_when.if_yes: File against the standard detail; no engineered design is submitted.
applies_when.if_no: A masonry or concrete wall that leaves the standard detail — slope over 10 percent, adverse soils, or any design departure — needs plans by a California registered design professional. A wood, vinyl or wrought-iron fence is outside this bulletin and is not held to that engineered-plan demand.

items.detail: The City's standard detail is all-or-nothing: an applicant relying on it may not modify any portion of it. The June 2026 revision uses the 2025 CBC and ASCE 7-22 with a 95 mph basic wind speed, exposure C. It is designed for the average condition, at an allowable soil bearing pressure of 1,500 psf with passive bearing at 100 psf per foot and footings a minimum 12 inches into undisturbed natural soil. Where the site slope exceeds 10 percent, where soil conditions are adverse — expansive soil, liquefaction, flood hazard — or where the design departs from the detail in any way, a design professional registered in California prepares the plans instead.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), LIMITS OF APPLICABILITY STANDARDS: "Use of this document shall not permit the applicant to modify any portion(s) of these details", and the purpose statement naming slopes steeper than 10%, adverse soil conditions and deviation from the bulletin (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Property corners monumented by a licensed surveyor before construction

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

items.detail: A licensed surveyor locates and monuments the property corners before construction starts. This is a pre-construction gate rather than a counter item, so its absence is a condition to satisfy, never a reason to refuse the packet.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 9: "Property corners shall be monumented (located) by a licensed surveyor prior to starting the construction" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Surveyor certification for a wall or fence within three feet of a property line

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Is any part of the new wall or fence within three feet of a property line?
applies_when.if_yes: For a masonry or concrete wall, submit the county-recorded corner monumentation by a licensed land surveyor or civil engineer. For a wood, vinyl or wrought-iron fence, submit the surveyor's setback certification, or the notarized waiver signed by each adjoining owner.
applies_when.if_no: No surveyor certification is submitted for a wall set back more than three feet from every property line.

items.detail: Within three feet of a property line the City draws a line by material. For a masonry or concrete wall, the affected property corners are located and monumented by a California licensed land surveyor or qualified licensed civil engineer and recorded with the county before building or rebuilding — and the survey waiver is not available for it. For a wood, vinyl or wrought-iron fence, a licensed surveyor instead certifies the setback, documenting the placement of the fence and posts relative to the property line, and is retained before construction to identify the property line. That certification lands before the footing inspection and the concrete pour. The waiver route exists only for the light-fence materials: a notarized Request to Waive Survey Requirement signed by each adjoining property owner, filed with the Building Division before the permit issues.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 10; Laguna Beach Request to Waive Survey Requirement for Fences Within 3 Feet of Property Line, which states the masonry monumentation-and-recording rule, the light-fence setback-certification alternative, and the notarized adjoining-owner waiver (June 2026 bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; waiver form verified live 2026-08-20)

items.label: Clearances to fire hydrants and water meters

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

items.detail: No wall or fence within 36 inches of a fire hydrant. No wall, fence or foundation within 12 inches of a water meter. The meter clearance reaches the footing, not only the wall above it, which is the part a plan most often misses.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 7: "No wall or fence shall be allowed within 36\" of a fire hydrant and no wall, fence, or foundation shall be allowed within 12\" of a water meter" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: No projection into the public right-of-way

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Does any part of the wall, its footing or its cap sit in the public right-of-way without an approved Revocable Encroachment Permit or Public Works encroachment permit that covers it?
applies_when.if_yes: Keep the whole wall, including any stone cap or trim, on private property, or obtain the encroachment approval first.
applies_when.if_no: Nothing is asked: the wall is clear of the right-of-way, or an approved encroachment permit covers the part in it. Staff confirm the approval covers this wall.

items.detail: Nothing projects into the public right-of-way, and the City names the decorative elements specifically: a stone cap or trim counts as a projection even where the wall face itself is clear. The rule yields to an encroachment the City has approved. A Revocable Encroachment Permit may allow "minor structures such as low fences and retaining walls" in an unimproved, unused right-of-way, and Public Works permits work within the right-of-way. When an approved REP or Public Works encroachment permit covers this wall, the wall or cap in the right-of-way is the approved condition; staff confirm the approval covers this wall and its cap.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 11: "No projections allowed in the public right of way including stone cap or trim" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27); Laguna Beach Revocable Encroachment Permit Application (updated July 2026), page 1: a REP "may allow minor construction in an otherwise unimproved, unused public right-of-way" for "minor structures such as low fences and retaining walls, walkways, stairs"

items.label: Site wall stands alone and retains nothing

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Is this wall filed against the City's Standard Block Wall Detail rather than an engineered design?
applies_when.if_yes: The wall must stand alone and retain nothing. A standard-detail wall drawn retaining grade, or tied into a structure, needs an engineered design instead.
applies_when.if_no: Omit it for an engineered retaining wall or engineered site wall, and for a wood, vinyl or metal fence.

items.detail: The standard detail covers a freestanding site wall: it retains no soil and forms no part of a building or other structure. A wall filed against the standard detail that is shown retaining grade, or tied into a structure, has left the bulletin and needs an engineered design. It never applies to an engineered retaining wall, which is the residential-retaining-wall case, or to a wood, vinyl or metal fence.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 12: "Site wall is standing alone. No retaining is permitted form part of building or other structure" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Combined wall and attachment height at or under six feet

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Does the design mount a railing, guard or screen on top of the wall?
applies_when.if_yes: The plan dimensions the combined wall-plus-attachment height from the lowest adjacent grade and keeps it at or under 6 feet 0 inches.

items.detail: A railing, guard or screen may not sit on the wall where the wall plus the attachment exceeds 6 feet 0 inches above the lowest adjacent grade. The measurement is the combined height from the lowest adjacent grade, not the wall height alone.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTE 13: "No railing, guard, or screen attachments are permitted where the wall height plus the rail, guard, or screen height exceed 6'-0\" above lowest adjacent grade" (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Solid grouting, bond pattern, cleanouts and expansion joints called out

scopes.label: Fence, gate or freestanding block wall

applies_when.question: Is this a concrete block or masonry wall?
applies_when.if_yes: Call out solid grouting of the CMU, running-bond pattern, cleanouts for lifts greater than 4 feet, and expansion joints at no more than 30 feet.

items.detail: The wall is solid grouted. Both footing alternates on page 2 of the June 2026 revision label the wall 6" MIN. CMU (SOLID GROUTED); the April 2020 revision labelled it only 6" MIN. CMU. A partially grouted wall that would have passed against the older sheet no longer matches the standard detail. Blocks are laid in running bond so head joints in successive courses offset horizontally by at least a quarter unit length. Cleanouts are provided for all lifts greater than 4 feet. Expansion joint spacing does not exceed 30 feet. The cleanout note is the one that bites in the field, because it is checked at the reinforcing steel inspection before grouting — the same inspection that makes solid grouting verifiable.

source.citation: Laguna Beach Standard Block Wall Detail (Information Bulletin, revised June 2026), GENERAL NOTES 4, 5 and 6, and the page-2 section callouts labelling both footing alternates 6" MIN. CMU (SOLID GROUTED) (City-issued applicant bulletin attached by City permit staff on 2026-08-26; the City's published copy, document 5099, still served the April 2020 revision when checked 2026-08-27)

items.label: Fence construction details show materials, design, specifications, post layout, fasteners and finishes

applies_when.question: Is this a wood, vinyl, wrought-iron or metal fence rather than a masonry or concrete wall?
applies_when.if_yes: Staff look for construction details identifying the fence material and design, the applicable specifications, post layout, fasteners and finishes.
applies_when.if_no: Nothing is submitted for this staff check on a masonry or concrete wall; the published Standard Block Wall Detail supplies those construction gates.

applies_when.question: Is this a wood, vinyl, wrought-iron or metal fence rather than a masonry or concrete wall?
applies_when.if_yes: Staff look for how each post attaches to the ground and for bracket specifications.
applies_when.if_no: Nothing is submitted for this staff check on a masonry or concrete wall; the published Standard Block Wall Detail supplies those construction gates.

applies_when.if_yes: Accept the stamp for permit issuance; the survey condition is handled in the field.

Decide whether this filing's work is part of the scope of a listed permit that is open or recently issued. A deferred submittal, a revision to approved plans, or a supplement that names that permit is part of it. A different project on the same parcel is not. Decide from the two descriptions; never from a permit prefix, a date, or a shared word. When the filing names another permit that the block does not list, or the block is absent, name the permit from the filing in the same question.
